nodes.name: HGT Formation by Carbonization
nodes.procedure: A certain proportion of FeCl3·6H2O and NiCl2·6H2O (Fe:Ni = 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:0, molar ratio) was first weighed and dissolved in ethanol. Subsequently, a certain mass of TPCA was added to the solution (the ratio of the total mass of FeCl3·6H2O and NiCl2·6H2O with the mass of TPCA is 1:3). After stirring thoroughly, it was dried at 80°C and then carbonized in N2 atmosphere at 800°C with a ramping rate of 5°C min⁻¹ to obtain the hollow graphite tubes containing FeNi alloy (Fex-Niy@HGT, x:y = 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:0 corresponding to Fe₂Ni₁@HGT, Fe₁Ni₁@HGT, Fe₁Ni₂@HGT, and Fe@HGT, respectively).

nodes.name: PBA Deposition on HGT
nodes.procedure: Firstly, FexNiy@HGT was dispersed in 0.1 M K₄[Fe(CN)₆] solution and stirred for 2 h. Later, the diluted HCl was added dropwise to the solution until the solution pH reached 1. After being aged for 24 h, the precipitate was centrifuged. Following drying overnight at 80°C, the final products FexNiyHCF@HGT were obtained (x:y = 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:0, corresponding to Fe₂Ni₁HCF@HGT, Fe₁Ni₁HCF@HGT, Fe₁Ni₂HCF@HGT and FeHCF@HGT, respectively).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe_xNi_y@HGT shows graphitic carbon (002) peak at 26.3° with d-spacing 0.34 nm, and Fe-Ni alloy (111), (200), (220) peaks at 43.6°, 50.8°, 74.7° proving good crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a is the XRD pattern of Fe_x Ni_y@HGT with different Fe/Ni ratios. The presence of graphitic carbon (002) crystalline planes is evidenced by the sharp peak located at 26.3° [26], and the corresponding layer spacing is calculated to be about 0.34 nm by the Bragg equation [27]. Meanwhile, the sharp diffraction peaks at 43.6°, 50.8°, and 74.7° are indexed as (111), (200), and (220) crystalline planes of the Fe-Ni alloy (JCPDS NO. 47-1405), proving its good crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe_xNi_yHCF@HGT shows typical PBA cube structure diffraction peaks between Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 and Ni2[Fe(CN)6] with no bifurcation/shoulder peaks indicating homogeneous double high-spin (Fe-N and Ni-N) crystal; average grain sizes calculated by Scherrer formula: 31.9 nm (Fe2Ni1HCF@HGT), 24.8 nm (Fe1Ni1HCF@HGT), 22.4 nm (Fe1Ni2HCF@HGT).
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the deposition of PBA on Fe_xNi_y@HGT, a series of typical diffraction peaks appear in the XRD pattern (Fig. 2a), attributed to the PBA cube structure. According to Scherrer formula (S3 in SI) [29], the average grain sizes of PBA were calculated to be around 31.9 nm for Fe2Ni1HCF@HGT, 24.8 nm for Fe1Ni1HCF@HGT, and 22.4 nm for Fe1Ni2HCF@HGT. ... the three strong diffraction peaks corresponding to the (200), (220), and (400) planes, are found between those of Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 (JCPDS NO. 01-0239) and Ni2[Fe(CN)6] (JCPDS NO. 46-0908), and there are no bifurcation or shoulder peaks in the diffraction peaks, indicating that the as-formed material is a homogeneous double high-spin (Fe-N and Ni-N) crystal rather than a physical mixture of the two PBAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe1Ni1@HGT shows lattice spacing of 0.207 nm corresponding to Fe-Ni alloy (111) crystalline plane and carbon layer spacing of 0.341 nm belonging to graphitic carbon (002) plane, consistent with XRD results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A lattice spacing of 0.207 nm was observed in the HRTEM (Fig. 1f-g), corresponding to the (111) crystalline plane of Fe-Ni alloy, and the carbon layer covered on its surface has a spacing of 0.341 nm, belonging to the (002) crystalline plane of graphitic carbon, which is well consistent with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of C, N, Fe, and Ni in Fe1Ni1@HGT and Fe1Ni1HCF@HGT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element mapping diagram in Fig. 1h-i indicates the uniform distribution of C, N, Fe, and Ni in the tube and the presence of the Fe-Ni alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe1Ni1@HGT shows absorption peaks at 1630 cm⁻¹ (C=C, C=N stretching) and 1401 cm⁻¹ (C-H, C-N stretching); after PBA deposition on Fe_xNi_yHCF@HGT, strong -C≡N- stretching peaks appear at 2080 and 2026 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3a, the absorption peak at 1630 cm⁻¹ is attributed to C = C and C = N stretching vibration, and the absorption peak at 1401 cm⁻¹ belongs to C-H and C-N stretching vibration in Fe1Ni1@HGT [31]. After in-situ deposition of Fe_xNi_yHCF, two strong absorption peaks appear at 2080 and 2026 cm⁻¹, due to the stretching vibration of -C ≡ N- [32].

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe_xNi_y@HGT shows D-peak (disordered carbon) at 1355 cm⁻¹, G-peak (graphitic sp² carbon) at 1597 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G < 1 proving good graphitization, and 2D-peak at 2700 cm⁻¹; after PBA deposition, new -C≡N- stretching peak at 2156 cm⁻¹ appears.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Raman spectra of Fe_x Ni_y@HGT (Fig. 3b), the strong characteristic peaks of carbon were observed, where the D-peak at 1355 cm⁻¹ represents the disorder of carbon, while the G-peak at 1597 cm⁻¹ is from the sp2 hybridization of carbon, representing the ordered graphitic structure. Thus the strength ratio of the two peaks (I_D/I_G) means the degree of graphitization of the carbon material [33]. The calculated I_D : I_G values in Fe_xNi_y@HGT are found to be less than 1, which proves good graphitization of the material. In addition, the broader peak appearing at 2700 cm⁻¹ is caused by the vibration of graphene-like carbon [34]. ... After PBA deposition, ... a strong new peak at 2156 cm⁻¹ appears, attributed to the stretching vibration of -C≡N- [35].

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe1Ni1@HGT shows Ni⁰ (852.8, 870.7 eV), Ni-N_x (858.3, 873.8 eV), Fe⁰ (708, 719.8 eV), Fe-N_x (710.9, 722.6 eV), N 1s: pyridine N (398.7 eV), Fe/Ni-N (399.9 eV), graphite N (401.5 eV, dominant), NO_x (403.0 eV); Fe1Ni1HCF@HGT shows Niᴵᴵ (856.4, 873.9 eV), Niᴵᴵᴵ (858.4, 875.5 eV), Feᴵᴵ (708.5, 721.3 eV), Feᴵᴵᴵ (710.0, 722.8 eV), strong -C≡N- in N 1s confirming successful PBA deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni element presents mainly in Ni⁰ state at 852.8 and 870.7 eV derived from Fe-Ni alloy, and the higher valence Ni at 858.3 and 873.8 eV derived from Ni - N_x substance [34,36]. After PBA deposition, Ni⁰ disappears, but Niᴵᴵ located at 856.4 and 873.9 eV and Niᴵᴵᴵ at 858.4 and 875.5 eV are observed [37]. Similarly, Fe exists mainly as Fe⁰ (708, 719.8 eV) and Fe - N_x (710.9, 722.6 eV) states in Fe1Ni1@HGT, and is transformed to Feᴵᴵ (708.5 and 721.3 eV) and Feᴵᴵᴵ (710.0 and 722.8 eV) at Fe1Ni1HCF@HGT [34,38]. The chemical states of N1s in Fe1Ni1@HGT include pyridine N (398.7 eV), Fe/Ni-N (399.9 eV), graphite N (401.5 eV), and NO_x (403.0 eV), respectively, with graphite N as the dominant form. ... After the deposition of PBA, the strong -C = N- bond appears in the XPS spectrum of N 1 s.
